examples.ko: 연착 안내 방송이 나오자 대합실이 술렁였어요.
examples.en: When the announcement about the delay came, the waiting room stirred.

examples.ko: 아이는 대합실에서 어머니를 찾자마자 울음을 터트렸어요.
examples.en: The child burst into tears as soon as he found his mother in the waiting room.

examples.ko: 대합실에 사람이 많아서 앉을 자리가 없어요.
examples.en: There are so many people in the waiting room that there is no seat.

examples.ko: 버스 터미널 대합실은 난방이 잘돼서 따뜻해요.
examples.en: The bus terminal waiting room is well heated, so it is warm.
I sat on a chair in the waiting room and read a book.
I went out to the station waiting room to meet my friend.

explain: 기차역이나 버스 터미널에서 차를 기다리는 곳이에요. 병원에서 기다리는 곳은 보통 '대기실'이라고 해요. 발음은 [대합씰]이에요.

phrases.example: 기차 시간이 될 때까지 대합실에서 기다렸어요.
phrases.en: I waited in the waiting room until the train time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역이나 터미널에서 차를 기다릴 때 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing for waiting for a train or bus at a station or terminal.
phrases.en_equiv: to wait in the waiting room

phrases.en: There are many people in the station waiting room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기차역' 안의 기다리는 곳이라는 뜻을 분명히 할 때 앞에 '역'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '역' (station) makes it clear it is the waiting area inside a train station.

phrases.en: I waited for the bus in the terminal waiting room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버스 터미널에서 차를 기다리는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the waiting area at a bus terminal.

explain_en: Large hall for travelers at stations and terminals. It is the place to wait for a train or bus at a station or terminal. The waiting area at a hospital is usually called '대기실'. It is pronounced [대합씰].

t90.ax: I sat on a chair in the waiting room and read a book.

examples.ko: 이 노선은 배차 간격이 너무 길어서 불편해요.
examples.en: This route is inconvenient because the interval between buses is too long.

examples.ko: 눈이 오는 날에는 배차가 자주 늦어져요.
examples.en: On snowy days the dispatch of vehicles is often delayed.

examples.ko: 회사에서 버스 배차를 조정한다고 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The company told us it is adjusting the bus schedule.

examples.ko: 밤에는 배차 시간이 한 시간으로 늘어나요.
examples.en: At night the interval between buses grows to one hour.
It took about ten minutes for the call taxi to be dispatched.

examples.ko: 배차는 승객이 많은 시간에 맞춰 짜는 거예요.
examples.en: The dispatch schedule is set according to the times when there are many passengers.

explain: 버스, 택시, 기차 같은 차를 정해진 시간에 보내는 일이에요. '배차 간격', '배차 시간'처럼 말하고, 일상에서는 '차가 자주 안 와요'라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: During rush hour, the interval between buses is short.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차가 오는 시간 사이의 간격을 말할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for the gap between vehicles.

phrases.en: I check the dispatch times on the app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차가 출발하는 시각을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the times when vehicles depart.

phrases.en: Please add more buses during rush hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운행하는 차의 수를 더 많게 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means increasing the number of vehicles in service.

explain_en: It means sending out buses, taxis or trains at set times. People say '배차 간격' and '배차 시간', and in daily talk may put it more simply as '차가 자주 안 와요'.

t90.ax: The company told us it is adjusting the bus schedule.

examples.en: Taking the shuttle bus to the airport is convenient.

examples.ko: 학교 앞에서 셔틀버스가 십 분마다 와요.
examples.en: A shuttle bus comes every ten minutes in front of the school.

examples.ko: 회사 셔틀버스 덕분에 출근 시간이 짧아졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the company shuttle bus, my commute got shorter.
The hotel runs a free shuttle bus.
I missed the shuttle bus, so I took a taxi.

examples.ko: 전시장으로 가는 셔틀버스는 역 앞에서 타요.
examples.en: You catch the shuttle bus to the exhibition hall in front of the station.

explain: '셔틀버스'는 학교, 회사, 공항, 행사장처럼 정해진 두 곳 사이를 왔다 갔다 하는 버스예요. 일반 시내버스와 달리 정해진 사람만 타거나 무료인 경우가 많아요. 줄여서 '셔틀'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Take the shuttle in front of the station.
phrases.nuance_ko: '셔틀버스'를 줄인 말로 말할 때 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened, casual form of 셔틀버스.

phrases.en: The shuttle bus stop is in front of the main gate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 셔틀버스가 서는 곳을 물을 때나 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask about or tell where the shuttle stops.

phrases.en: There is a free shuttle bus to the event site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 셔틀버스는 무료인 경우가 많아서 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shuttle buses are often free, so this phrase is common.

explain_en: 셔틀버스 runs back and forth between two set places like a school, workplace, airport, or event site. Unlike regular city buses, it is often free or only for certain people. People also shorten it to 셔틀.

examples.en: You must turn on your headlights on a night road.
My headlight is broken, so I'm going to get it repaired.
When you enter a tunnel, the headlights turn on automatically.

examples.ko: 맞은편 차의 전조등 때문에 눈이 부셨어요.
examples.en: The headlights of the oncoming car dazzled me.
The headlight was dim, so I changed the bulb.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 낮에도 전조등을 켜는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: On rainy days it's good to turn on the headlights even in the daytime.

explain: 자동차 앞쪽에서 길을 비추는 불이고, 말할 때는 영어식으로 '헤드라이트'라고도 많이 해요. 차 뒤쪽의 불은 '후미등'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I turned on the headlights before entering the tunnel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어두운 길이나 터널에서 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for dark roads or tunnels.

phrases.en: I turned off the headlights after parking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '켜다'의 반대로, 불을 없앨 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 켜다, used when switching the lights off.

phrases.en: The headlights were so bright that they dazzled me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 영어식 말로, 일상 대화에서 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: An English-based word with the same meaning, heard more often in daily talk.

explain_en: Formal or technical term for vehicle headlight (안전 안내) It is the light at the front of a car that lights the road, and in speech people also often say '헤드라이트' (headlight). The lights at the back of a car are called '후미등'.

t90.ax: The headlight was dim, so I changed the bulb.

en: to leave a room; to check out

examples.ko: 기숙사는 규칙을 어긴 사람에게 퇴실을 요구할 권한이 있어요.
examples.en: The dorm has the authority to ask rule-breakers to leave.

examples.ko: 독서실에서는 입실 시간과 퇴실 시간을 꼭 기록해야 해요.
examples.en: At the study room you must write down your entry and exit times.
Hotels usually require you to check out by 11 a.m.
I plan to check out this afternoon.

examples.ko: 퇴실하기 전에 방을 깨끗이 정리해 주세요.
examples.en: Please tidy up the room before you leave.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝난 사람은 먼저 퇴실해도 돼요.
examples.en: People who have finished the exam may leave the room first.

explain: 독서실, 기숙사, 호텔, 시험장처럼 정해진 방에서 나올 때 쓰는 말이고, 반대말은 '입실하다'예요. 호텔에서는 '체크아웃하다'라고 더 자주 말해요. 병원에서 나올 때는 '퇴원하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Check-out time is eleven in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방에서 나가야 하는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The time by which you must leave the room.

phrases.en: I checked out of the hotel at ten.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호텔에서는 '퇴실하다'보다 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more than '퇴실하다' at hotels.

phrases.en: Time is up, so please leave the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방에서 나가 달라고 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request to leave the room.

explain_en: Leaving a hotel, hospital, or study room by a set time. This is used when leaving an assigned room such as a study room, dorm, hotel or exam hall, and its opposite is '입실하다'. At hotels people more often say '체크아웃하다'. When leaving a hospital, you use '퇴원하다' instead.

examples.en: A donation box is placed in front of the station.
The students put a little of their allowance into the donation box.
They held a donation box and asked for help on the street.

examples.ko: 카페 계산대 옆에 작은 모금함이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small donation box next to the cafe counter.

examples.ko: 모금함은 한 달에 한 번 열어서 확인해요.
examples.en: We open the donation box once a month to check it.
The donation box was full too, so we had to empty it.

explain: 연말에 구세군 냄비나 편의점, 학교에서 보는 것처럼 기부금을 넣는 통을 말해요. '모금함에 넣다', '모금함을 설치하다'처럼 써요. 사람들에게 돈을 모으는 일 자체는 '모금'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I put a thousand won into the donation box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기부하는 사람의 행동을 말할 때 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for what a donor does.
phrases.en_equiv: to put into a donation box

phrases.en: The school set up a donation box at the library entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모금하는 쪽 입장에서 통을 두는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: From the side of those collecting, meaning placing the box.
phrases.en_equiv: to set up a donation box

phrases.example: 연말이 되면 거리에 구세군 모금함이 보여요.
phrases.en: At year end you see Salvation Army donation boxes on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연말에 거리에서 보는 대표적인 모금함을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the typical year-end street donation box.

explain_en: It refers to a box where you drop donations, like the ones seen at year-end charity drives, stores and schools. It is used as '모금함에 넣다' or '모금함을 설치하다'. The act of collecting money itself is called '모금'.

examples.ko: 미납금이 있으면 서비스를 이용할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't use the service if you have an unpaid balance.

examples.ko: 이번 달 안에 미납금을 내 주세요.
examples.en: Please pay the outstanding balance within this month.
I got a text message about an unpaid bill.

examples.ko: 관리비 미납금은 벌써 세 달 치예요.
examples.en: The unpaid maintenance fees already add up to three months.
Late fees are added to unpaid amounts.

examples.ko: 미납금을 한꺼번에 내기 어려우면 나눠서 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If it's hard to pay the overdue amount all at once, you can pay in installments.

explain: 요금, 세금, 관리비처럼 내야 하는데 아직 내지 않은 돈이에요. 고지서나 안내 문자에서 자주 보고, '미납금을 납부하다', '연체료'와 같이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '밀린 돈'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I paid the unpaid bill at the bank today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미납금을 내다'보다 공식적인 말로, 고지서나 안내문에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal way to say 'pay the unpaid bill', often seen on notices and bills.

phrases.example: 밀린 돈이 있어서 이번 주에 내려고 해요.
phrases.en: I still owe some money, so I plan to pay it this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미납금'을 일상 대화에서 쉽게 풀어 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain, everyday way to say 'unpaid bill' in conversation.

phrases.en: A late fee is added to unpaid bills.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미납금을 늦게 낼 때 더 내는 돈으로, 미납금과 함께 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The extra money you pay for paying late; it often appears together with 'unpaid bill'.

explain_en: Money you owe that is still unpaid; bills, fees (저는 아직 내지 못한 미납금을 이번 주 안에 모두 낼 거예요.) It refers to money such as fees, taxes or maintenance charges that should have been paid but hasn't. You see it on bills and notice messages, often alongside '미납금을 납부하다' (pay the overdue amount) and '연체료' (late fee). In casual talk people also say '밀린 돈' (money in arrears).

examples.en: I went to my friend's wedding and gave a monetary gift.
I don't know how much to give as a monetary gift.
I sent condolence money to my friend's father's funeral.

examples.ko: 부조금 봉투에 이름을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must write your name on the money envelope.
At work, we collected money from the staff separately as a gift.

examples.ko: 부조금은 축하나 위로하는 마음을 담아 내요.
examples.en: People give this money to express congratulations or comfort.

explain: 결혼식이나 장례식처럼 큰일이 있는 집에 돕는 마음으로 내는 돈이에요. 결혼식에는 '축의금', 장례식에는 '조의금'이라고 나누어 말하기도 해요. 보통 봉투에 넣어서 내요.

phrases.en: I gave 50,000 won as a wedding gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼식 같은 기쁜 일에 내는 돈만 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Money given only for happy events like weddings.

phrases.en: I gave condolence money at the funeral.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장례식처럼 슬픈 일에 내는 돈만 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Money given only for sad events like funerals.

phrases.example: 결혼식이 끝나고 부조금을 받은 봉투를 정리했어요.
phrases.en: After the wedding, I sorted the envelopes with the gift money.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내다'는 주는 쪽, '받다'는 받는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 내다 is from the giver's side; 받다 is from the receiver's side.

explain_en: General gift money for weddings or funerals; broader term. It is money given to a family holding a big event, such as a wedding or funeral, as a way of helping out. People often distinguish '축의금' for weddings and '조의금' for funerals. It is usually handed over in an envelope.

examples.en: Yesterday I sent my parents some money.
You can send money easily with the app.
I send money right after I get paid.
There's a fee to send money overseas.
If you give me your account number, I'll send the money right away.
I sent money to the wrong person by mistake.

explain: 은행 계좌에서 다른 계좌로 돈을 보내는 것을 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '이체하다'도 쓰는데, '이체'는 은행 서비스 이름처럼 자주 보이고 '송금'은 상대에게 보낸다는 느낌이 강해요. 현금을 직접 주는 건 '주다', 택배로 보내는 건 '부치다'예요.

phrases.en: I transferred the rent to the landlord's account.
phrases.nuance_ko: '송금하다'와 비슷하지만 은행 앱이나 은행 서비스에서 더 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '송금하다', but seen more often in bank apps and services.

phrases.en: Please send the money to this account by today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 돈을 보내 달라고 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask someone to send money.

phrases.en: The fee for sending money abroad is expensive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 보낼 때 은행에 내는 돈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The fee paid to the bank when sending money.

explain_en: It means sending money from your bank account to someone else's. 이체하다 is a close synonym that you see more in banking menus, while 송금하다 stresses sending to a person. Handing over cash is 주다, and mailing something is 부치다.

examples.en: At the end of every month, I go around to clients and collect unpaid bills.

examples.ko: 지방에 푼 물건값을 수금하려고 출장을 갔어요.
examples.en: I went on a business trip to collect payment for goods sent out to the provinces.
The secretary took on the job of collecting dues.

examples.ko: 이번 달 요금은 다음 주에 수금할 예정이에요.
examples.en: We plan to collect this month's charges next week.

examples.ko: 직원이 가게를 찾아와 월세를 수금해 갔어요.
examples.en: A staff member came to the shop and collected the monthly rent.
It isn't easy to collect old unpaid bills.

explain: 돈을 받는 쪽에서 '받을 돈을 받아 모으다'라는 뜻으로 써요. 회비를 걷는 정도의 일상적인 일은 보통 '걷다'를 써서 '회비를 걷다'라고 말해요. 돈을 내는 쪽은 '내다', '납부하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Today I collected the outstanding payment from the client and came back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 받아서 돌아오는 흐름을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for collecting money and bringing it back.

phrases.en: The shop owner came to get the unpaid bill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '수금하다'보다 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say 수금하다.

phrases.en: We collected the membership fees at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임 같은 일상적인 상황에서는 '걷다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday situations like a club meeting, 걷다 is used.

explain_en: Collect payments or dues (회비를 수금하다) It is said from the receiving side, meaning to gather money that is owed to you. For everyday things like collecting dues, people usually use '걷다' instead, as in '회비를 걷다'. The paying side uses '내다' or '납부하다'.

examples.en: There is a test drive of the new car this afternoon.

examples.ko: 시승을 해 보고 나서 차를 사기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to buy the car after taking a test drive.

examples.ko: 시승은 예약한 사람만 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people who made a reservation can take a test drive.
The reporters who took part in the test drive left their reviews.
The test drive reviews were good, so I went with high expectations.

examples.ko: 이번 시승 차량은 새로 나온 전기차예요.
examples.en: This test-drive car is the newly released electric car.

explain: 사려고 하거나 새로 나온 차를 직접 타 보는 것을 말해요. '시승을 하다', '시승 행사', '시승 후기'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '시운전'은 만들거나 고친 차를 시험 삼아 운전해 보는 것이라 차이가 있어요.

phrases.en: A new car test-drive event will be held this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 직접 타 볼 수 있게 마련한 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an event set up so people can try driving a car themselves.

phrases.en: I chose a car after reading test-drive reviews.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 타 본 사람이 쓴 경험담이나 평가를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an account or evaluation written by someone who has test-driven a car.

phrases.en: I called the dealership and applied for a test drive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 타 볼 기회를 미리 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you request a chance to test-drive a car in advance.
phrases.en_equiv: to sign up for a test drive

explain_en: It means actually riding or driving a car you are thinking of buying or a newly released car. It appears in '시승을 하다', '시승 행사' and '시승 후기'. The similar '시운전' is about trial-running a car that was just built or repaired, so it differs.

examples.ko: 서류를 우송하는 데 보통 이삼 일이 걸려서 일정에 여유를 두었어요.
examples.en: Mailing documents usually takes two or three days, so I left some leeway in the schedule.
I'll mail the contract to your address tomorrow.

examples.ko: 책을 우송하려면 먼저 포장부터 해야 해요.
examples.en: To mail the book, you need to wrap it first.

examples.ko: 합격 증서를 집으로 우송했다고 연락이 왔어요.
examples.en: I got word that they mailed the certificate of acceptance to my home.
I received the documents you mailed today.
I'll mail the item this afternoon.

explain: 우편으로 보낸다는 점이 분명한 딱딱한 말이라 공문이나 안내문에서 많이 나와요. 일상에서는 '부치다'나 '보내다'를 쓰고, 택배로 보낼 때는 '택배로 보내다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Please mail the documents to this address.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우편으로 보내 달라고 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request to send something by mail.

phrases.en: The book was mailed yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 우편으로 보내지는 입장에서 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This passive form focuses on the item being sent by mail.

phrases.en: I sent the package by mail.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우송하다'를 일상 말로 풀어서 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday way to say the same thing as 우송하다.

explain_en: It is a formal word that makes clear something goes by post, so it appears in official notices. In daily life people say '부치다' or '보내다', and for courier delivery '택배로 보내다'.

examples.en: I pay rent by automatic transfer.
How much is the transfer fee?

examples.ko: 이체가 아직 안 된 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems the transfer hasn't gone through yet.
Making a transfer with the app is convenient.
I went over today's transfer limit.

examples.ko: 이체 내역은 앱에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see your transfer history in the app.

explain: '이체'는 은행 계좌에서 다른 계좌로 돈을 보내는 것이에요. 말할 때는 보통 '송금'이나 '입금'을 더 많이 쓰고, '이체'는 은행 앱이나 '자동 이체'처럼 은행 용어로 자주 보여요. 다른 사람에게 돈을 보내면 송금, 받는 쪽에서 돈이 들어오면 입금이에요.

phrases.en: Can I pay by bank transfer?
phrases.nuance_ko: 카드나 현금이 아니라 계좌로 돈을 보내는 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the payment method: sending money by account, not card or cash.

phrases.en: I checked the transfer history in the app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 보낸 기록을 말하고 은행 앱에서 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: The record of money sent; often seen in banking apps.

phrases.example: 다른 은행으로 보내면 이체 수수료가 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a transfer fee if you send to another bank.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 보낼 때 은행에 내는 돈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The fee you pay the bank when sending money.

explain_en: Moving money between accounts (자동 이체) 이체 means moving money from one bank account to another. In conversation people more often say 송금 or 입금, while 이체 shows up in bank apps and in 자동 이체. Sending money to someone is 송금, and money arriving on the receiving side is 입금.
